Snapalabra! - Learn Languages Through Images.


Visual Learning: Learn through carefully curated images that create lasting memory connections

Smart Clues: Contextual hints that help you write and speak with confidence

Smart Flashcard System: Interactive post-it style cards with flip animations and progress tracking

Speech Recognition: Practice pronunciation with built-in text-to-speech technology



Key Features That Make Learning Fun:

Interactive Flashcards: Beautiful, animated cards that flip to reveal translations
Image-Based Learning: Visual cues that help you remember words forever
Progress Tracking: Monitor your learning journey with detailed analytics
Contextual Clues: Hints that guide you on your path to fluency 

Perfect For:

Students learning new languages
Travelers preparing for trips abroad
Business professionals expanding global communication skills
Language enthusiasts wanting to master multiple tongues
Anyone who learns better through visual methods

How It Works:

Choose Your Languages: Select your native and target languages
Browse Images: Explore curated images with language context
Explain what you see: Using the provided clues, try explain what you see through either speech or text.

Master Languages: Build vocabulary through visual repetition

Privacy & Security:

Your learning data stays private and secure
No personal information shared with third parties
GDPR compliant data handling
Secure authentication with Firebase

quotes.text:
Working on a visual language learning app called Snapalabra!

The idea is simple: You look at an image and describe what you see in your target language. That's basically it!

My reason for building it was that even though I can understand a lot of spoken spanish, I really struggle to construct sentences on the fly when speaking. Doing a few minutes of active learning like this each day really helps remap my brain a little, and I quickly run into situations where I hit a wall and realize I actually don't understand something as well as i had thought.

The app also gives a little feedback on what i have written from an llm, and it also provides clues that I have mapped to each image.

At the moment I am using it mainly for intermediate Spanish and beginner Irish, and personally I find it really helpful for both. Basically learning vocan for Irish, and more serious sentence structure etc. in Spanish.

I know a lot of people absolutely hate the idea of mixing LLMs with language learning, and I can kind of see why, but I personally find it really helpful in certain cases. If you are already doing classes, and consuming content in your target language I think something like this will be really helpful for a 5 minute coffee-break type activity in the morning. Its not a language course and I have not intention for it to be one. Its just a supplementary little tool that helps with getting your brain thinking in a new language and it is free to use.

quotes.text:
Just a simple app I created to to help myself with learning vocabulary contextually, and to give myself an opportunity to get instant feedback on mistakes I make in my target language.

The idea is simple: Describe an image in your target language. To help you, there are clues mapped to the image. You can interact with those clues to get example sentences, or listen to the words. Once you describe the image, you can get some (LLM) feedback. I know this is not for everyone but I personally find it super helpful. And it will also generate some smart flashcards (if you are logged in) based on any mistakes you make.

Hope you enjoy, and thanks for reading!

Also available for ios/android:

Google play: https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.whatever555.snapalabra.

App store: https://apps.apple.com/us/app/snapalabra/id6747401847

The app provides some helpful features to assist in your learning. There are clues mapped to the image, some LLM feedback (if you are into that), and it generates some smart flashcards based on your spelling mistakes.

quotes.text:
Hello all,

I’d love to get some feedback on an app I’ve been working on called Snapalabra.

The idea is simple: each day you get a new image, and you describe what you see in your target language. That’s it — a small, focused daily expression exercise.

To help, the app provides image-mapped clues, and there’s an optional LLM feedback feature (I know that’s not for everyone) that can suggest ways to expand on what you've written or spoken.

It’s not a course and doesn’t try to be one. It’s just a dedicated space to practice expressing yourself alongside whatever other language learning you're already doing — Spanish, German, Basque, French, Irish, or anything else.

I built it because I felt a big gap between what I could understand and what I could express. Even as my comprehension improved, I’d still freeze when trying to form sentences. Forcing myself to produce a few sentences every day helped “rewire” my brain and make sentence structure and vocabulary easier to recall.

So far I’ve really enjoyed both using and building it, and I’m excited to keep refining the concept.

App Store: https://apps.apple.com/us/app/snapalabra/id6747401847

Play Store: https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.whatever555.snapalabra

Web: https://snapalabra.com

The app is built with Flutter for Android and iOS.

Thanks for reading!
